question: Does automated-looking traffic to the website repository rise promptly after new commits are made visible on Forgejo?
publication_time_priority: commit committer time as explicitly labeled proxy only
unit: Push batch, not individual commit or individual request; simultaneous commits share publication exposure.
primary_cohort: Existing linux-chrome-150-155 rule: X11; Linux x86_64 with Chrome/150 or Chrome/155. This is a user-agent heuristic, not verified bot identity.
primary_outcome: Successful GET repository web responses, excluding known maintenance/check agents and Git smart-protocol transfers.
window_rule: Compare the 30 whole minutes before the push minute with the 30 whole minutes after it; omit the push minute to avoid rounding and completion-time ambiguity.
primary_statistic: Mean post-minus-pre request count per push batch.
null_reference: 10000 random common circular minute shifts of the push train within each occupied UTC date/hour block, leaving the request series fixed; preserve batch sizes and within-hour event spacings up to wraparound.
null_assumption: Conditional exchangeability of push minutes within date/hour blocks under no prompt response. This is an observational timing test, not randomized treatment assignment.
coverage: Require observed log coverage, available surrounding windows, and a stable Anubis phase; omit October 4 and windows crossing recorded difficulty/cookie transitions. Log spans alone do not certify continuous uptime.
sensitivity_checks: Isolated batches with no other push within 60 minutes
Successful requests of all user agents
All response statuses in the primary cohort
Other repositories as a negative-control outcome
5, 60, and 180 minute windows with Holm correction across these secondary window tests
additional_evidence: First requests for explicitly named commit hashes relative to recorded pushes
Daily and hourly commit/request associations, labeled descriptive and confounded
Distribution of requested commit age and historical-versus-new targets
interpretation_guardrails: Commit creation time is not push/publication time.
Several commits arriving in one push cannot establish one independent trigger per commit.
Correlated requests and overlapping windows do not create independent replication.
Time-of-day coincidence, policy changes, and activity accompanying publication can confound interpretation.
Absence of a detected effect does not prove absence of monitoring.
If publication history or coverage is inadequate, report the limitation rather than substitute an unqualified significance claim.
